Method of Attack: Customized ransomware attacks demanding ransom payments
Encrypts files using AES encryption and embedded RSA key
Harvests unencrypted files from victims' servers and publishes them on a data leak site
Sells access to victim's internal network along with stolen data
Spreads laterally within networks to gain Windows domain administrator credentials
Attack Vector: Human-operated ransomware attack involving network breach and lateral movement
Use of Windows domain administrator credentials to spread and execute ransomware
Indicators of Compromise: Ransom note named HELP_SECURITY_EVENT.html in each folder
Ransom demands range from $500,000 to $700,000 in Bitcoin
Dedicated Tor payment sites per victim
Data leak site listing victims and publishing stolen data
Commands involving wmic, schtasks, and execution of ScreenCon.exe from domain controller
